newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-JOHNSON IN ENGLAND SQUAD FOR AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-JOHNSON IN ENGLAND SQUAD FOR AUSTRALIA.

text.p: British Lions captain Martin Johnson has been named in a 27-strong England squad for the one-off test against Australia in Sydney on July 12.
But the Rugby Football Union, who announced the squad on Monday, said that a decision on his fitness would not be made until after the third test against South Africa a week earlier.
"There is still a doubt about Martin Johnson because of the need to rest a groin injury following the Lions tour. He will make his own decision following the third test," a statement said.
If Johnson is fit he will be joined by all 20 of the Lions' England contingent who will fly direct from Johannesburg.

A decision on the final line-up will not be made until the squad arrives in Sydney, but it is sure to show changes from the side which lost to Argentina earlier this month as nine of that team have failed to make the trip.
Phil de Glanville, overlooked by the Lions, retains the captaincy.
The most notable absentees are scrumhalf Andy Gomarsall and wing Jon Sleightholme who have been overtaken by Matt Dawson and John Bentley.

Backs: Tim Stimpson, Nick Beal, Adedayo Adebayo, John Bentley, Tony Underwood, Phil de Glanville (captain), Will Greenwood, Jeremy Guscott, Mike Catt, Alex King, Kyran Bracken, Matt Dawson, Austin Healey.

Forwards: Tim Rodber, Tony Diprose, Richard Hill, Lawrence Dallaglio, Ben Clarke, Neil Back, Martin Johnson, Simon Shaw, Nigel Redman, Mark Regan, Phil Greening, Darren Garforth, Jason Leonard, Graham Rowntree.
